recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-25278 unless PA or Patient Care later opens a separate decision on Appointment.reason Procedure guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-25278 asked whether Appointment.reasonReference should point to request resources because appointments are commonly scheduled before the associated procedure exists. The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution distinguished Appointment.reason from Appointment.basedOn and directed adding MedicationRequest, DeviceRequest, and CarePlan to Appointment.basedOn.
initial_application: Git commit 6363f23c2f7c79b1c14a3fe3a5efa484a5c48d7f explicitly applied FHIR-25278 by changing Appointment.basedOn wording from service request to request and adding CarePlan, DeviceRequest, and MedicationRequest beside ServiceRequest.
additional_context: Appointment is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source keeps Appointment.reason as a CodeableReference to clinical reason resources and uses Appointment.basedOn for request/authorization references. Later FHIR-40634 expanded Appointment.basedOn with additional request-like targets without removing the FHIR-25278 targets. PA WGM minutes and the linked Zulip thread support the same reason-vs-basedOn interpretation.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source edit is needed. The current combined branch already has CarePlan, DeviceRequest, and MedicationRequest in Appointment.basedOn, and adding those request references to Appointment.reason would conflict with the accepted resolution.

related_jiras.note: Later PA change broadened Appointment.basedOn with additional request-like targets while preserving CarePlan, DeviceRequest, and MedicationRequest.
O&O device boundary issue mentioned during PA discussion; it clarifies Device/DeviceRequest usage generally but does not change Appointment.basedOn.
